newsitem.title: USA: U.S. lawmakers seek change in budget laws.
newsitem.headline: U.S. lawmakers seek change in budget laws.

text.p: A bipartisan group of more than 200 Republican and Democratic lawmakers on Wednesday sought a major revision of the way the federal budget is developed, including a provision to prevent future government shutdowns.

Rep. Christopher Cox, Republican of California, said the plan would require Congress to pass a one-page budget by April 15. Unlike current budgets, it would be sent to the White House for signature and would bind the government to its spending and taxation levels.
The current budget process was started in 1974 and Congress has regularly missed its April 15 deadline to develop a complete federal budget.

Cox said the legislation would require spending limits be set in 20 broad categories, except for Social Security. Once the budget was signed into law, it would require a two-thirds vote of the House and Senate to spend more.

If Congress and the president fail to pass any of the appropriations bills before the October 1 start of a new fiscal year, those programs would be continued automatically at the previous year's funding. Social Security and interest on the national debt would be exempted from automatic funding.
